name: You become like the company you keep
meaning: Good company clears the mind, puts truth into speech and raises one's honour; the same drop of water vanishes on hot iron and becomes a pearl in a shell.
applies_when: Someone is choosing friends, a peer group, a workplace or a partner's circle, or noticing how others are shaping them.
misleads_when: It is used to look down on people, or to cut off someone who simply needs help.
modern_application: List the five people you spend most time with. For each, ask whether you are clearer, kinder and more honest after time with them. Spend a little more time with those who raise you up.

name: The marks of a true friend
meaning: A true friend keeps you from wrong, joins you to what is good, keeps your secrets, makes your virtues known, stays in trouble and gives at the right time.
applies_when: Someone is unsure whether a friendship is good for them, or wants to be a better friend.
misleads_when: It is used to demand perfection from friends, or to keep a secret that endangers someone's safety.
modern_application: Check one friendship against the six marks. Then check yourself as a friend against them, and do one of them this week.

name: Keep your distance from those who harm
meaning: A harmful person is to be avoided even if learned, as a snake adorned with a jewel is still dangerous; friendship with the wicked starts big and dwindles.
applies_when: Someone is drawn to, or stuck with, a person who repeatedly harms, manipulates or demeans them, especially one who is charming or impressive.
misleads_when: It is used to label someone 'wicked' after a single conflict, or to refuse any possibility of change.
modern_application: Forgiving someone does not require staying close to them. Decide what distance keeps you safe and well, and hold it kindly but firmly.

name: Give it, enjoy it, or lose it
meaning: Wealth has three courses: giving, enjoyment and loss; whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
applies_when: Someone is hoarding out of fear, or unsure what their money is for.
misleads_when: It is used to discourage prudent saving for real needs, or to justify reckless spending.
modern_application: Split what you can spare this month three ways: something to give, something to enjoy, and something to keep for a stated purpose.

name: A cut tree grows again
meaning: A tree that is cut grows again, and the waning moon fills again; reflecting on this, the good are not crushed by misfortune.
applies_when: After a loss, failure or setback, when someone fears they will never recover.
misleads_when: It is used to rush someone through grief, or to deny that some losses are permanent.
modern_application: Recall one earlier time you recovered from something you thought would break you. Write down what helped then.

name: Character is the real ornament
meaning: Each quality has its ornament (restraint of speech for courage, humility for learning, giving for wealth), but character is the highest ornament of all.
applies_when: Someone is focused on appearance, status or possessions to feel worthy.
misleads_when: It is used to shame people about how they look or what they own.
modern_application: Choose one quality you want people to remember you for, and practise it deliberately in one interaction each day.

name: Do not leave the just path, whatever others say
meaning: Let the clever blame or praise, let wealth come or go: the steadfast do not stray a step from the path of justice, and the best never give up what they have begun, however often obstacles strike.
applies_when: Someone is under pressure to compromise their integrity, or to abandon a worthwhile effort because of setbacks or criticism.
misleads_when: It is used to persist in a course that is clearly harming oneself or others, or to dismiss honest feedback.
modern_application: Write down the principle you will not trade away in this situation. Decide in advance what you will say when pressed.

name: Effort is the friend; laziness the enemy
meaning: Laziness is the great enemy inside the body; there is no friend like effort, and one who keeps working does not sink. Even if results follow past actions, the wise act after careful thought.
applies_when: Someone is waiting for luck or fate to change their situation, or has slipped into inertia.
misleads_when: It is used to blame people whose struggles come from illness, injustice or circumstances beyond their control.
modern_application: Pick the one action that is fully in your hands today, and do it before anything else.

name: Much is decided beyond our effort
meaning: Bhartrihari's verses on fate say that even the mighty fall, that what is not destined will not happen, and that past deeds ripen in their time.
applies_when: An adult, not in distress, who has done all they can, needs to accept an outcome they could not control, without blaming themselves.
misleads_when: It turns into fatalism that stops effort or acceptance of help, or is used to say people deserve their suffering. Never offered to anyone in distress or under 18.
modern_application: Separate what you did from how it turned out. Accept the outcome you could not control, and keep the lesson you can use.

name: Say the unwelcome thing that helps
meaning: Pleasant talkers are easy to find; rare is the person who says what is unpleasant but good for you, and rarer still the one who listens. Even wise words fail when spoken at the wrong time.
applies_when: Someone must give or hear honest feedback, warn a friend, boss or relative, or is avoiding a conversation because it will be uncomfortable.
misleads_when: It is used to excuse cruelty or bluntness for its own sake, or to press a point when the moment is wrong or the person is in crisis.
modern_application: Write the one sentence the other person needs to hear. Check it is true and that it helps them, not you. Then choose a calm, private moment to say it.

name: Do not do to others what you would not want done to you
meaning: Vidura sums up dharma in one line: do not do to another what is disagreeable to yourself. Meet anger with calm, meanness with giving and falsehood with truth.
applies_when: Someone is tempted to retaliate, cut a corner at another's expense, or is unsure how to treat a person who has treated them badly.
misleads_when: It is used to tell someone to keep accepting harm, or to deny that protecting oneself from an abuser is right.
modern_application: Before you act, swap places: picture this being done to you. If you would object, choose the response you would want instead.

name: Stand by your relatives
meaning: Relatives can carry you across or pull you under. Help a relative who is poor, sick or struggling; share meals, talk and affection with them, not quarrels.
applies_when: Someone faces a family rift, an inheritance or support dispute, or a relative in need, and wonders how much they owe.
misleads_when: It is used to keep someone in contact with an abusive or dangerous relative, or to demand support that a person cannot give. Safety comes first.
modern_application: Name one relative who is struggling. Do one small, concrete thing this week: a call, a meal, an errand, or an honest talk to end a quarrel.

name: Be fair to those who work for you
meaning: People stay loyal in hard times to a leader who does not rage at them and does not cut their pay to court newcomers. Plan the work and the fair wage first, then gather the right helpers.
applies_when: Someone manages people, hires or lets people go, sets pay, or runs a team, shop or household with staff.
misleads_when: It is used to excuse keeping someone who harms others, or to expect loyalty without paying what is due.
modern_application: List the people who work for or with you. Check that each is paid on time and fairly, and that you have not taken your frustration out on any of them. Fix one thing this week.

name: Trust with care
meaning: Do not trust the untrustworthy, and do not trust even the trustworthy blindly; the harm that comes through trust cuts to the roots.
applies_when: Someone is deciding whether to lend money, share a secret, sign something, or rely on a new partner, friend or colleague.
misleads_when: It turns into suspicion of everyone, or stops someone from asking for help when they need it.
modern_application: Before you hand over money, passwords or secrets, ask: what happens if this trust is broken? Keep that risk to a size you can afford.

name: Act so you will not regret it later
meaning: Since life is uncertain, do not start what you would grieve over on your deathbed. Everyone errs; the wise set right what remains.
applies_when: Someone faces a choice with lasting consequences, or has made a mistake and asks what to do now.
misleads_when: It feeds endless second-guessing or guilt, or is offered to someone overwhelmed by regret instead of support.
modern_application: Imagine yourself much older, looking back on this choice. Which option would that person be glad you took? If you have already erred, name one thing you can still set right.

name: Dislike colours what we see
meaning: Someone we dislike never seems good, clever or learned; we see good deeds in those we like and bad ones in those we dislike.
applies_when: Someone is judging a person they resent, such as a rival, an in-law or an ex, and wants to know if they are being fair.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss real harm someone has done as 'just your bias'.
modern_application: Write down three things the person you dislike has done well. If you cannot, ask someone neutral. Then judge the one action in front of you on its own.
